A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Learn2Mix and provide readable text, equations, three figures, three tables, and appendices A–C. Content can be matched reliably across the changed layout and numbering.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original classification, regression, and reconstruction experiments, with numerical results and learning curves in Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original experimental results across classification, regression, and reconstruction, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same training loop, loss-based mixing updates, and cyclic class-specific sampling. Shortened algorithm comments and helper names do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six classification benchmarks, three regression datasets, and three image-reconstruction datasets. The balanced and manually imbalanced scenarios are unchanged, including the dataset descriptions in Appendix B.

E2.justification: Classification comparisons retain classical training, focal training, and SMOTE. Regression and reconstruction retain classical training as the comparator. No comparator is added or removed from the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C retain the same splits, imbalance construction, metrics, epoch budgets, architectures, and hyperparameters. Table 2's label change from 'Err' to 'MSE' clarifies the existing metric.

E4.justification: The same convergence curves, training-versus-test comparisons, and class-imbalance analyses remain. No ablation, sensitivity study, robustness test, or supplementary case analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same uncertainty-reporting practice: ± annotations in Tables 1–2 and shaded bands in Figures 2–3. V2 adds no run or seed counts, uncertainty definitions, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain all numerical results, and the learning-curve images are identical. For example, final Learn2Mix IMDB accuracy remains 82.33±0.50 and California Housing MSE remains 0.77±0.08. Reported convergence findings also match.

T1.justification: Definitions 2.1–2.2, Propositions 2.3 and 2.5, Corollary 2.4, and their appendix proofs retain the same mathematics and assumptions. V2 numbers the existing final proof inequality as Equation 61, shifting subsequent equation numbers without adding a result.

C1.justification: The adaptive-mixing, conditional-convergence, and empirical efficiency contributions remain the same. Summary comparisons change 'classical' to 'existing' approaches, but the broader comparisons and associated claims already appear in v1's Section 4.1.

C2.justification: Both retain the same class-difficulty explanation, reduced-overfitting interpretation, and applicability to regression and reconstruction through categorical groups. V2 trims repeated conclusions without introducing substantive qualifications or limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain the dataset construction details, architecture specifications, focal-loss settings, SMOTE batch-matching procedure, and Table 3 hyperparameters. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to resampling, loss weighting, curriculum learning, and meta-learning remain the same. Citation-style and bibliographic-formatting changes do not introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited wording edits, shortens algorithm comments, corrects the first author's name, and revises affiliation text. It simplifies the proof heading from Appendix A.1 to A while preserving the main narrative and section sequence.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout. Existing figures and tables are enlarged and repositioned, algorithms and equations are reflowed, table labels are expanded, and the appendix gains a separate title block. The figure content itself is unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 primarily changes the template and lightly edits wording while preserving the methods, proofs, experiments, results, and reproducibility information. Larger plots and clearer table labels offer modest benefits, alongside heavier wrapping of equations and algorithms. These presentation tradeoffs do not produce a meaningful net change in overall quality.
